title: Integrals, areas and lengths as sums of small pieces: six workspaces, one habit of reading the readout
summary: Six Math Studio screenshots use the same pattern: split a region into n small pieces, add up one quantity per piece, and print the exact value and the error beside the sum. The pieces differ: grid cells with a Jacobian, spherical wedges, boxes, frustum bands, chords and polar cells.

media.alt: Screenshot of the Integrals Lab, change of variables. Left, a uv-plane with a six by six grid and one orange cell. Right, an xy-plane showing the grid mapped to a tilted square lattice with the image of the orange cell highlighted. A readout at the top lists the cell index, the image area (2.0), the Jacobian determinant (2.0), the sum 2.00000, the exact value 2.00000 and an error of 6.33e-13.

read_the_figure.question: What is the piece, what quantity is summed over pieces, and how does the printed error behave as the pieces shrink?
read_the_figure.axes: Each screenshot has a panel of controls on the left, a drawing in the middle (cells, wedges, boxes, bands, chords, polar cells), and a readout at upper right with sum, exact value and error. Some have a small log-log inset of error against n.
look_at: Change of variables: a cell of area du dv in the left plane is mapped to a parallelogram of area |J| du dv on the right. The readout confirms: image area 2, |J| = 2, sum equal to the exact value.
Spherical wedges: the volume of a shell 1 <= rho <= 2 as 18 x 6 x 6 wedges; the sum is 29.62975 against the exact 29.32153 (28 pi / 3), error 0.308.
Boxes: the unit cube cut into 6 x 6 x 6 = 216 boxes, mass sum 1.50000 for density x + y + z, error 2e-15: a linear density is integrated exactly by midpoint boxes.
Polar cells: the disk r = 2 cos(theta), 24 radial cells per ray, sum 4.710171 against exact 4.712389, error 0.0022; the readout also checks that moving the pole does not change the integral.
Surface bands: a sphere cut into 8 frustum bands, band sum 49.299645 against exact 50.265482 (error 0.966), while the wrong 'cylinder bands' give 39.478.
Arc length: 6 chords in a cardioid give a polygon length of 7.115225 against exact 8.0: the chord length is always below the arc, error 0.885. The inset shows the error falling with slope minus 2.
read_the_figure.proves: The same sum-and-limit idea gives areas, volumes, masses, surface areas and lengths; the printed errors show convergence, and the exact values give an independent check. The pieces must be the right ones: chords always underestimate, cylinder bands converge to the wrong surface area.
if_wrong: A sum that converges to a different number than the exact value: the element of area or volume is wrong (missing Jacobian, rho squared or r).
An error that does not decrease with n: a systematic error, not a discretization one.
A polygon longer than the curve: impossible for chords of a rectifiable curve.
A surface area formula using 2 pi y dx instead of 2 pi y ds: converges, but to the wrong value.
must_check: That the element (area, volume, length, surface) is stated in the formula line.
That the exact value is printed next to the sum.
That n and the cell size are visible.
That an error inset, if present, has log-log axes and its slope is quoted.

terms.meaning: The factor by which a change of variables scales area or volume.
The volume of the small piece: rho squared sin phi d rho d phi d theta in spherical coordinates.
A small piece of a disk bounded by two radii and two rays; its area is r dr d theta.
A band of a surface of revolution approximated by a cone slice; lateral area pi (r1 + r2) times the slant length.
A polygon through points on a curve; its length is a lower bound for the arc length.

remember: The element matters: dA = |J| du dv, dA = r dr d theta, dV = rho^2 sin phi d rho d phi d theta.
Surface area uses arc length ds, not dx: S = integral of 2 pi y ds.
Chords always underestimate arc length; the error falls like 1 over n squared.
A midpoint rule integrates a linear function exactly.
Compare the sum with an exact value whenever the exact value is available.

steps.title: Change of variables
steps.tex: \iint_R f\,\mathrm dx\,\mathrm dy=\iint f\bigl(x(u,v),y(u,v)\bigr)\,|J|\,\mathrm du\,\mathrm dv,\quad J=\det\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}
steps.note: For x = u + v, y = u - v the Jacobian is -2, so |J| = 2, which is exactly what the readout prints.

steps.title: Spherical shell
steps.note: The exact value printed. The 18 x 6 x 6 wedge sum is about 1 percent high, because midpoint sampling of sin(phi) over six steps overestimates it (sin is concave).

steps.title: The polar disk
steps.note: Matches the exact value in the polar panel. The factor r in the area element is what the 'forget the r' checkbox deletes to show the error it causes.

steps.title: Archimedes' hat-box and the wrong bands
steps.tex: S=\int2\pi y\,\mathrm ds=4\pi R^{2}=50.265\ (R=2),\qquad \int2\pi y\,\mathrm dx=\pi^{2}R^{2}=39.478
steps.note: Using dx instead of the slant length ds converges to 39.478, the 'cylinder bands' value in the readout, not to the area of the sphere.

steps.title: Arc length of the cardioid
steps.note: Six chords give 7.115 (checked by computing the chord lengths between six equally spaced angles). The chord length is shorter for every n.

worked.title: The Jacobian of the first screenshot
worked.problem: For x = u + v, y = u - v find |J| and the image area of a cell of area 1/36 (six by six grid on the unit square).
worked.answer: |J| = 2, so each cell's image has area 1/18 and the whole unit square has image area 2, as the readout says.

analyze.q: Why does the boxes screenshot have an error of 2e-15 and the wedges one 0.3?
Describe the effect of forgetting the r in the polar cell sum.
Why must a chord polygon be shorter than the curve?
analyze.hint: Straight line is the shortest path.

evaluate.q: Two sums converge to different numbers. How would you decide which is right using only the readout?
evaluate.hint: Compare with the exact value; check the element.

evaluate.q: The error panel shows slope -2. What does that predict if n doubles?

create: Choose f and a region for which the polar and Cartesian integrals are both easy and confirm they agree.
Derive the frustum band area formula from the area of a cone and check it for a cylinder.

checks.answer: The factor by which a small area is scaled by the change of variables.

checks.q: dV in spherical coordinates at rho = 2, phi = pi/2, with d rho = d phi = d theta = 0.1?
checks.hint: rho^2 sin phi times the product.

checks.q: Why does the spherical wedge sum exceed the exact volume here?
checks.answer: Midpoint sampling of sin phi over six steps overestimates it by about 1.1 percent (sin is concave), and midpoint sampling of rho squared underestimates by about 0.1 percent; the net is about +1.05 percent, which is what 29.630 against 29.322 shows.

checks.q: Cylinder bands give 39.478 for a sphere of radius 2. Why is this not a rounding problem?
checks.answer: Because the sum converges to a different integral: 2 pi y dx instead of 2 pi y ds; more bands do not fix it.

checks.q: Make a seventh workspace panel for the same pattern: what piece, quantity and exact value would you choose?
checks.answer: Moment of inertia of a disk by polar cells: piece r dr d theta, quantity r^2 times density, exact pi R^4 / 2 times density.
